title: Hack Back Email
coreMove: Turn email from a constant cue into a batched commitment with clear next handling rules.
sourcePressure: The chapter narrows work-interruption logic into the inbox, treating email as a repeat trigger system that needs bounded handling and norms.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would chase inbox zero prestige or declare email evil instead of building bounded response paths.

hook: Hack Back Email as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: rural clinic administrator sorting lab-supply emails
exampleSpecs.audience: administrator whose inbox steals vaccine inventory time
exampleSpecs.stakes: orders need accuracy more than instant vendor replies
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she moves vendor promos to a Friday buying batch and handles only the expiring reagent notice now
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A reagent expiry sheet lies beside a filtered vendor email.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent game composer receiving revision emails
exampleSpecs.audience: composer who lets each note pull him out of scoring
exampleSpecs.stakes: fragmented attention makes the cue list worse
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he creates two revision windows and parks nonblocking notes in the score-change folder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A MIDI controller sits beside a score-change folder.

exampleSpecs.domain: university lab manager handling equipment requests
exampleSpecs.audience: manager copied on every supply question
exampleSpecs.stakes: urgent repairs and routine requests need different paths
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she replies with two routing labels, repair-now and next-order, then closes the inbox until the batch
